description: For the pool operator, as the daily check and the first stop when a dingo-forging alert fires. Answers: will every Dingo block producer forge its next block, and did it forge the ones it was due? The header is the verdict. Below it: one table line per producer that exists now; what became of every leader slot, who made the blocks and whether any producer is overdue for one; when each producer's next leader slot is, how far it is through this epoch's schedule and whether every scheduled slot became a block (these need a newer Dingo and say so until it runs); where a forge's time goes against the 1 s slot; and whether each producer could forge at every moment. Bad looks like: invalid credentials, any sign or dial failure, a leader slot that did not become an adopted block, an opcert counter behind the chain, few KES periods left, a stuck or halted ledger pipeline, a sign round trip near its sign timeout, or tip lag that keeps climbing. Only DingoNodes that load forging credentials are shown; relays are left out, and so is a producer that no longer exists at the end of the time range, even where its old samples are still inside it. Agent panels cover only producers that sign through a KES agent.

panels.description: One ring per producer: the time since its last adopted block, measured against its own typical gap between blocks (observed time divided by blocks adopted over the last 7 days, or since the producer appeared). The ring fills as the wait grows and is full at five typical gaps; the two ticks mark one and three. Leader slots are a lottery, so gaps vary a lot: a wait of three typical gaps happens about 5% of the time and five about 0.7%, which is what the last line under each ring works out for the current wait (hover a ring for the block count behind its typical gap). **Healthy: green rings, under three typical gaps.** Amber from three, red from five: that long without a block is unlikely to be luck, so check that the producer is at tip, its credentials are valid and its pool is still registered with stake. The typical gap comes from recent history, not from stake, because Dingo does not export the pool's stake; a producer with only a few blocks in 7 days has a rough estimate. The 7-day look-back is fixed and does not follow the dashboard range.

panels.title: Leader Schedule: Next Slot and Epoch Progress

panels.description: One bar per producer for the dashboard range: every leader slot it was scheduled for, split by what became of it. **Green** adopted as its own tip. **Amber** forged, then not adopted. **Red** the leader check was won and no block was forged (the reason is in Forge Problems). **Dark red** a scheduled slot the slot clock passed that the forger never checked, because the node was syncing or on a stale tip at that moment (`dingo_leader_scheduled_slots_elapsed_total` minus leader checks won): this is the true missed-slot count, and it is invisible to every older counter. **Grey** yielded to another pool of the same node that led the same slot, which is not a loss. The line under the bar is the funnel in numbers, then the slot-battle record: battles settle a security parameter of blocks after they are detected, as *won* (the pool's block stayed on the chain) or *lost* (`dingo_forge_slot_battle_outcomes_total`). *Detected* also counts slots a rival took before this node forged, which never settle, so won plus lost can be lower. **Healthy: solid green bars.** Losing a slot battle is the lottery of two pools sharing a slot, not a fault, unless one producer loses most of them (then look at its block propagation). Counters start with the process: slots that passed while a node was down are in no counter, so compare *scheduled* in the panel beside this one with the blocks adopted in the epoch. Until a newer Dingo runs, the bars start at leader checks won and the panel says what is missing.

panels.title: Schedule vs Reality: Scheduled Slot to Adopted Block

panels.description: One bar per producer: the mean time to forge a block over the dashboard range, drawn against the 1 s slot and split into its stages. **Blue** is everything the producer does itself around the signature (leader check, building the block, adopting it locally; for local-KES producers also the KES sign). For producers that sign through the KES agent the sign round trip (`dingo_kes_agent_sign_latency_seconds`) is split with the agent's own timings: **orange** network and TLS, **grey** the KES sign inside the agent, **purple** the Postgres slot-guard write that blocks double signing. **Green** is the producer's self-validation of the block. Total is `dingo_metrics_blockForgingLatency_seconds` (leader check to local adoption). The right-hand figure is the mean and its share of the slot; the line under the bar gives each stage and the latest forge. Means, not percentiles: a producer forges a few blocks a day. **Healthy: under 250 ms, a small fraction of the slot**; amber from 250 ms, red at 1 s, where the block is late for its own slot. A long purple segment is the slot guard's database, a long orange one the path to the agent. Only producers that exist now are drawn. With more producers than fit, the panel drops the stage line (hover a segment instead) rather than scroll.

panels.title: Forge Anatomy: Where a Block's Time Goes

panels.description: One row per producer, coloured by the worst state it was in during each step. In order of severity: **credentials invalid** (it cannot sign), **pipeline stuck** (ledger pipeline stuck or halted), **syncing** (over 600 slots behind the wall clock), **lagging** (300 to 600 slots behind), **agent session idle** (a producer that signs through the KES agent holds no open session; informational, because the session is redialled before a leader slot), **ready**. A gap means the producer did not exist. **Healthy: green, with thin pale gaps on agent producers at most.** A red or blue stretch across a leader slot is a lost block; a long idle stretch together with dial failures below means the producer cannot reach the agent.

panels.description: Time per forged block, as the mean over 15-minute windows, so one point is one block (or the average of the blocks in that window). **Total forge** (blue) runs from the leader check to local adoption; **KES sign round trip** (orange) is the part spent waiting for the KES agent, for the producers that use it; **self-validation** (green) is the producer checking its own block. Points are drawn because blocks are sparse, and the histogram buckets are too coarse for quantiles at a few blocks an hour. The shaded bands are the budget: amber from 250 ms, red from the 1 s slot. **Healthy: every point below the amber band**; when a blue point is high, the orange point under it shows whether the agent round trip is the cause.

panels.description: Everything that stops a leader slot from becoming a block, per hour: leader slots missed after selection, slots where forging failed, a KES agent sign that failed, forged blocks that failed the producer's own validation, forges refused by the last-forged-slot fence (the guard against forging the same slot twice after a restart), and forge attempts skipped because the node was syncing or its tip was stale (with the reason). With a newer Dingo it also shows **scheduled slots never checked**: leader slots the slot clock passed while the forger was refusing to forge (`dingo_leader_scheduled_slots_elapsed_total` minus leader checks won). A skip is counted every slot the node is behind; a scheduled slot never checked is a block actually lost to it. Series at zero are hidden, so **a flat baseline is the healthy state**. Any bar is a lost block: read the producer log for that hour.

panels.title: Forge Problems

panels.description: Per hour: failed dials or handshakes to the agent, and moves from one agent address to another. **Healthy: all flat at zero.** A failover with no dial failure afterwards is a replica restart handled cleanly. Dial failures that continue mean no replica is reachable from that producer. **Signer not ready** (a newer Dingo): a producer opens its agent session three slots ahead of a leader slot; this counts the leader slots where that preparation failed (`dingo_forge_remote_kes_signer_not_ready_total`). The sign at the slot dials again, so it is a warning that the block was at risk, not a lost block: a lost one shows as an agent sign failure in Forge Problems.
